It's true that a malformed-JSON error here is what triggers the leak by skipping the rest of the function, but `json.loads` itself doesn't manage any file resource. The actual defect is upstream: the file was opened with a bare `open(path)` instead of a `with` block, so nothing guarantees cleanup once this line raises.

`f.close()` is the right cleanup call and works fine as long as execution reaches it, so tapping it doesn't identify the flaw. The real issue is that this line can be skipped entirely if `json.loads` raises earlier, which only a `with open(path) as f:` block would prevent.
